title: DR + AWS Backup — RTO/RPO and centralized backup policies

answers.explanation: RPO = max acceptable data loss window — 30 minutes of wiki views (Night 19 block 1).
RTO = max acceptable outage — 15 minutes to restore wiki availability drives warm standby vs backup-restore.
Backup and restore = cheapest DR tier with highest RTO — AWS Backup + IaC redeploy (four-strategy ladder).
Warm standby runs scaled-down live DR; pilot light keeps minimal core only — lower RTO for warm standby.
AWS Backup centralizes multi-service policies — Night 18 Q10 preview; PITR is per-table only.
Tag-based selection auto-enrolls matching resources — night-19-lab saa-study-backup=night-19 pattern.
Aurora Global Database for sub-second cross-Region RPO — Night 15 Q5 trap (not promote read replica).
CloudTrail audits API calls — not a backup service (Night 18 Q10 / Night 19 exam traps).
Copy action moves recovery points to destination vault on schedule — not live replication.
Global tables = live multi-Region writes; AWS Backup copy = discrete recovery points.
Backup vault stores encrypted recovery points — saa-study-gsa-backup-vault in night-19-lab.
On-demand backup job or manual snapshot before risky migration — complements scheduled plans.
Night 19 teardown deletes vault/plan/recovery points only — Night 18 table unchanged (mirrors Night 18 Q15).
Multi-site active-active for near-zero RTO/RPO — DynamoDB global tables + regional endpoints.
Native Aurora backups are per-service; AWS Backup adds centralized retention across resource types.
